findings.conditions: Pr>1 process grid; one process row finishes its L-solve and the row-scope Allreduce while a process P in the same process column but another row is still in its L-solve loop
findings.reasoning: The L-solve and U-solve both use tags Xk/LSUM on grid->comm, and both receive with MPI_ANY_SOURCE/MPI_ANY_TAG. Between them the only synchronisation is MPI_Allreduce over the row scope (grid->rscp) that computes brecv; there is no grid-wide barrier. A diagonal process of a U-solve root supernode k in a row that has already passed the Allreduce Isends Xk(k) down process column kcol right away. P, in another row, may still be in the L-solve wildcard receive. It takes that message as an L-solve X block, runs dlsum_fmod with U-solve data and decrements nfrecvx/fmod. It then leaves the L-solve with one genuine L message unconsumed, which the U-solve loop later takes as a U message. The result: a corrupted lsum/x and a wrong solution, or a hang or bad index when the counts stop matching.

findings.conditions: Iterative refinement in pdgsrfs_ABXglobal with Pr>1; a row finishes its L-solve early and the U-solve roots send Xk to a lagging process in another row
findings.reasoning: This is the same structure as pdgstrs_Bglobal. The L-solve (lines 380-490) and the U-solve (line 798 onward) reuse the tags Xk and LSUM on grid->comm and receive with MPI_ANY_SOURCE/MPI_ANY_TAG. The only thing between them is a row-scope MPI_Allreduce/MPI_Reduce for brecv, and the L-solve Isends are MPI_Request_free'd without waiting. U-solve root processes immediately Isend Xk to the processes in their column, and those processes may sit in other rows that are still in the L-solve loop. The L-solve receive then takes a U-solve X block, applies L(i,k)*x with the wrong vector, decrements nfrecvx/fmod, and leaves a genuine L message for the U-solve to misinterpret. The correction dx comes out wrong, or the counts go out of step.

findings.conditions: Follows a misdirected U-solve Xk taken by the L-solve loop on a lagging process (no grid-wide barrier between L- and U-solve)
findings.reasoning: This is the U-solve half of the same race. When the L-solve wildcard receive on process P has consumed an early U-solve Xk message, P exits the L-solve with one genuine L-solve Xk (tag Xk, from another diagonal process of its column) still pending. The U-solve wildcard MPI_Recv(ANY_SOURCE, ANY_TAG) then matches that leftover L-solve message as a U-solve X block and calls dlsum_bmod with L-solve y data, decrementing nbrecvx/bmod. The tags are identical, so nothing detects the mismatch, and x comes out wrong, or the bmod counts underflow or stall.

findings.conditions: Complex ABglobal driver, Pr>1, a row enters the U-solve while another row of the same process column is still in the L-solve
findings.reasoning: The complex-precision copy of pdgstrs_Bglobal has the same flaw: the L-solve MPI_Recv(MPI_ANY_SOURCE, MPI_ANY_TAG) on grid->comm and the U-solve sends use the same tags Xk/LSUM, separated only by a row-scope Allreduce. A U-solve Xk Isent by a root diagonal process can be matched by the still-running L-solve loop of a process in another row of the same column. That loop treats it as L-solve data, which leads to a wrong solution, or a hang if the counters go out of step.

findings.conditions: Parallel symbolic factorization, intra-level block pipeline; a size message for a later block, or the dummy self-send, matches the pending wildcard Irecv
findings.reasoning: The size messages are received with MPI_Irecv(MPI_ANY_SOURCE, tag_intraLvl_szMsg), and that tag is the same for every block of the level. When the count from prvP shows that all messages have already arrived, the pending wildcard Irecv is 'cancelled' by a self-send of a dummy value. If any real size message with that tag can reach this process before the self-send, the wildcard receive takes it. It is then thrown away, and the dummy is later taken as a real size message, so MPI_Recv(rcvP=self, tag_intraLvl_LData) never matches and the process hangs. The token chain seems to rule this out in normal operation, hence the low confidence.
